scripts: The CloudFormation template: IAM users and groups with no permissions attached.
Checks the account, then creates the stack. Asks you to confirm the account first.
Removes only the lab stack and what you added to its users and groups.

blocks.p: Use an account you created for practice. **Never run the scripts in an employer's account.** The seed script stops if an account has more than 50 IAM users. IAM, CloudFormation and CloudShell have no charge.

Seeding and cleanup create and delete IAM users, groups and a CloudFormation stack. Use an administrator rather than the root user. The check only reads, so it also runs as a user or role with the AWS managed `ReadOnlyAccess` policy.
Choose the CloudShell icon in the console's top bar. CloudShell runs with your console sign-in, so no access keys are created or stored. Use the same Region for every script; the stack lives there.

setup.title: Download the files and upload them to CloudShell

blocks.p: In CloudShell, choose **Actions > Upload file** for each one. Read the scripts before you run them; each explains what it does at the top.
The dry run checks the account and lists what would be created, without changing anything. The seed then asks you to type the account ID:
It creates the CloudFormation stack `rolevara-lab`: 7 IAM users and 9 IAM groups under the path `/rolevara-lab/`, with no permissions attached, so the lab users can't do anything in the account.

run.title: Work the six tickets in the IAM console

blocks.p: Open **IAM > Users** and **IAM > User groups**. In IAM terms, an enabled account has **console access**, a leaver's sessions are revoked by **deactivating his access key**, and department and job title are the `Department` and `JobTitle` tags. The access matrix and runbook are on the [Policy & matrix](#/policy) page.
The check makes only describe, list and get calls and writes `rolevara-aws-export.json`. Download it with **Actions > Download file**, then open the **Upload results** tab:
You can fix things in IAM and check again as often as you like.
This removes what you added to the lab users (console passwords, keys, group memberships), then deletes the stack. It touches only users and groups under `/rolevara-lab/`.

todo.REQ0018841: Give Maria Lopez console access (autogenerated password) and add her to exactly the AP Clerk groups.
todo.REQ0018850: Offboard Robert Hayes: disable console access, deactivate his access key, and remove him from every group.
todo.REQ0018852: Move Tanya Wright to Operations / Dispatcher: edit her Department and JobTitle tags, swap Sales groups for Dispatcher groups.
todo.REQ0018870: Rehire Sofia Ramirez as HR / HR Generalist: enable console access with a new password, update her tags, remove old access, add the new role's groups.
todo.REQ0018879: Put Rachel Adams on leave: disable console access and keep her groups.
todo.REQ0018881: Provision Ethan Moore as a Dispatcher from the access matrix: enable console access and add the Dispatcher groups, not Bob Turner's.

trouble: The seed stops on accounts with more than 50 IAM users so it can't touch a real organization. If the account really is a lab, run it with `--lab-account`.
A previous lab is still there. Run `python3 remove_rolevara_lab.py`, then seed again.
"No 'rolevara-lab' stack in this account and Region"
CloudShell is in a different Region from the one you seeded in. Switch Regions in the console's top bar and open CloudShell again.

Seeding and cleanup need permission to manage IAM and CloudFormation, such as `AdministratorAccess`. The check needs only `ReadOnlyAccess`. See [AWS managed policies for job functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_job-functions.html).
Enabling console access fails on the password
Choose an autogenerated password. A custom one must meet the account's password policy.
Robert's access key still counts as active
Deactivating or deleting the key both count. Check that you changed the key on Robert Hayes, under **Security credentials**.
The check says a user "was not found"
The user was deleted. The runbook removes access instead, so that ticket scores 0. Remove the lab and seed it again to retry.
Run `python3 remove_rolevara_lab.py` again. It retries and removes what is left.
The upload says the file isn't a lab export
Upload `rolevara-aws-export.json` from the check script. If you edited it, check again.
